forces.title: Rise of Intelligent, Sovereign, and Scalable Financial Operating Systems
forces.description: India's financial sector is shifting towards intelligent operating systems, integrating AI, trusted data, programmable money, and digital public infrastructure (DPI). This transformation enables autonomous, resilient, and inclusive financial services. For market infrastructure, this means adapting to real-time decision-making, interpreting context, executing transactions, and managing risk in real-time. This broad shift, supported by India's DPI foundation, will fundamentally redefine how exchanges, depositories, and clearing houses operate, pushing for greater efficiency and automation.

forces.title: Tokenization and Programmable Finance Reshaping Capital Markets
forces.description: Tokenization is emerging as a foundational layer for next-generation financial market infrastructure, enabling programmable transactions, atomic settlement, and greater interoperability. By representing deposits, securities, and other assets as digital tokens, it enhances market liquidity, broadens participation, increases transparency, and improves settlement efficiency and cost. This directly impacts exchanges and clearing houses by driving a need for modernized infrastructure capable of supporting 24x7 programmable liquidity services, smart collateral management, and near real-time settlement of digital assets.

forces.title: Increasing Investment in Digital Assets and Stablecoin Infrastructure
forces.description: There is significant global investment, particularly from corporate VC, shifting towards market control points and infrastructure within the digital assets space. This includes stablecoin and payment infrastructure, tokenization platforms, settlement networks, and custody services. For market infrastructure entities, this signifies a crucial development as traditional exchanges and depositories must either evolve to support these new asset classes and settlement mechanisms or face new competitors. The focus on interoperability between fiat and stablecoins also implies a need for modernised payment rails within the capital markets ecosystem.

forces.title: Massive Scale of Digital Public Infrastructure Driving Data Ecosystems
forces.description: India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), exemplified by UPI processing billions of transactions monthly and the Account Aggregator framework enabling data sharing for millions, creates one of the world's richest real-time financial-data ecosystems. This massive data scale and growing interoperability provide a strong foundation for AI-driven financial services, including within capital markets. For market infrastructure, this offers an upside by potentially feeding into enhanced data analytics for index providers, enabling more sophisticated risk management for clearing houses, and supporting more agile trading platforms.
forces.source_title: Beyond automation: How AI is reshaping the next decade of banking

forces.title: Growing Retail Participation and Demand for Leveraged Equity Exposure
forces.description: Sustained retail participation in Indian capital markets is evidenced by an eightfold increase in demat accounts from FY17-26 and robust growth in the Margin Trading Facility (MTF) book. This demographic shift, with more financially active post-COVID savers investing in equities and mutual funds, directly drives trading volumes and the demand for financing products like MTF. For exchanges and clearing houses, this represents a significant tailwind for transaction fees and the overall scale of market activity, contributing to revenue growth and market depth.
forces.source_title: MTF Scales New Peak; While ADTO Declines

forces.title: Tighter RBI Regulations and Higher Transaction Costs Impacting Derivatives
forces.description: Recent tighter RBI funding norms for capital-market exposures have impacted leveraged and proprietary trading activity, leading to a sequential moderation in F&O Average Daily Turnover (ADTO). Additionally, higher transaction costs, partly due to SEBI's regulatory measures, are weighing on derivatives volumes. For exchanges, particularly those with a strong F&O segment like NSE, this poses a headwind to revenue generation from derivatives trading and could slow the growth of what has traditionally been a high-volume segment, requiring adaptation in product offerings or fee structures.
forces.source_title: MTF Scales New Peak; While ADTO Declines

forces.title: Cybersecurity and AI Threat Landscape Widening for Financial Infrastructure
forces.description: The rapid advancement of AI, particularly Generative AI, is significantly widening the industry's attack surface faster than most control environments can keep pace. Attackers can now automate phishing campaigns, vulnerability hunts, and social engineering at near-zero marginal cost. For market infrastructure entities (exchanges, depositories, clearing houses), this presents a critical key risk. Safeguarding digital identities, payments, and financial infrastructure against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats necessitates continuous investment in cybersecurity, robust governance frameworks, and federated fraud intelligence systems.
forces.source_title: Beyond automation: How AI is reshaping the next decade of banking

forces.title: Quantum Readiness Emerging as Critical Priority for Financial Security
forces.description: Quantum readiness is rapidly emerging as a critical strategic priority for financial institutions and infrastructure providers globally. The potential for quantum computing to break existing cryptographic security measures poses a long-term, high-impact risk to digital identities, payments, and the integrity of financial infrastructure. This necessitates significant investment in post-quantum cryptography, establishing quantum financial innovation hubs, and preparing for future technological disruption. Market infrastructure entities must proactively engage in these advancements to safeguard the security and trust of their systems.

forces.title: Shift Towards Autonomous and Real-Time Market Infrastructure Operations
forces.description: The financial services industry is moving towards AI-native operating models that integrate intelligence more deeply across operations. This includes agentic AI transforming financial services through autonomous decision-making in areas like fraud case-building, AML monitoring, and credit underwriting. For market infrastructure, this means evolving from manual or semi-automated processes towards more autonomous execution across investigations, monitoring, and decision-support tasks, underpinned by real-time data and advanced analytics. This requires substantial investments in technology, data modernization, and reimagined operating models.

forces.title: Subdued Market Sentiment and Global Uncertainties Weigh on Trading Activity
forces.description: In July 2026, cash-market Average Daily Turnover (ADTO) softened sequentially, declining by 8.2% month-on-month. This moderation primarily reflected subdued market sentiment, range-bound equity markets, and profit booking after a strong rally. Heightened global uncertainties, including geopolitical conditions and trade disruptions, also contributed to lower secondary-market trading activity. For exchanges, this represents a cyclical headwind to trading volumes, potentially impacting transaction fee revenues in the short term, despite a generally positive long-term structural outlook for investor participation.
forces.source_title: MTF Scales New Peak; While ADTO Declines

viewpoints.title: Tokenization and AI as core to future 24x7 financial market infrastructure
viewpoints.description: KPMG views tokenization and AI as foundational for next-generation financial market infrastructure. Tokenized deposits, money market instruments, and securities enable atomic settlement and programmable transactions, fostering greater interoperability and efficiency. This will drive financial institutions to compete on programmable liquidity services, smart collateral management, and 24x7 market infrastructure. AI, evolving towards autonomous systems, will transform banking from transaction-driven to proactive and personalized, with critical implications for how exchanges and clearing houses operate and process value.

viewpoints.title: MTF book growth positive long-term despite near-term moderation risks
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings holds a positive long-term structural outlook for the Margin Trading Facility (MTF) book, anticipating continued investor adoption and its increasing importance as a key revenue driver for stockbrokers. However, the firm notes a cautious near-term view, expecting MTF book growth to moderate due to prolonged market uncertainty, tighter regulatory conditions, elevated transaction costs, and heightened sensitivity to global geopolitical and macroeconomic developments. The sustained growth in leveraged equity positions highlights investor preference for such financing products.
viewpoints.source_title: MTF Scales New Peak; While ADTO Declines

viewpoints.title: India poised to lead global financial operating system redesign with DPI and AI
viewpoints.description: KPMG asserts that India is uniquely positioned to design the future financial operating system globally, leveraging its digital public infrastructure (DPI), technology talent, and policy ambition. The country's proven ability to build interoperable digital infrastructure at scale for its population, combined with emerging AI capabilities, programmable money, and trusted data, enables it to create an intelligent, sovereign, and scalable financial architecture. This leadership position is derived from demonstrated innovation in financial infrastructure and the potential to set global benchmarks.

demand_drivers.description: Government-led programs and digital platforms have significantly expanded access to formal financial services, encouraging broader participation in market-linked products like equities and mutual funds.
Increased digital connectivity and the availability of accessible market-linked products have attracted more households to formal financial markets, driving demat account growth.

market_sizing.methodology: Total count of demat accounts in India. This indicates expanding participation in formal financial markets, directly driving activity on stock exchanges and depositories. Source documents highlight an eightfold increase from 28 million in FY17 to 225 million in FY26.
market_sizing.source_title: India’s new insurance track: The marathon becomes an AI-led decathlon

demand_drivers.description: Continued involvement of retail investors in equity markets, driven by long-term structural factors, creates ongoing demand for leveraged positions.

demand_drivers.driver: Adoption of MTF as a financing product
demand_drivers.description: MTF is increasingly being adopted as a preferred financing avenue for equity trading, underscoring its growing importance for stockbrokers and, consequently, the market infrastructure supporting these trades.

market_sizing.methodology: Average value of the Margin Trading Facility (MTF) book as of July 2026, calculated from data on all Tuesdays and the last working day of each month. This represents the total leveraged equity exposure facilitated by brokers and cleared via market infrastructure.
market_sizing.source_title: MTF Scales New Peak; While ADTO Declines

demand_drivers.description: Comparisons to a subdued trading period in July 2025 (following previous regulatory tightening) contributed to the strong year-on-year growth figure.
Underlying structural factors continue to support investor engagement in the capital markets, providing a foundation for trading volumes.

pnl_drivers.description: New RBI regulations on capital-market exposures reduced leveraged and proprietary trading activity, leading to a sequential decline in F&O ADTO.
Increased costs associated with trading, partly due to SEBI's regulatory measures, contributed to the moderation in derivatives volumes.
General market sentiment, range-bound equity markets, profit booking, and heightened global uncertainties led to a sequential decrease in cash-market ADTO.

market_sizing.methodology: Average Daily Turnover (ADTO) across Futures & Options (F&O) and equity segments for July 2026. This metric reflects the daily trading activity on exchanges and is a key revenue driver for market infrastructure providers.
market_sizing.source_title: MTF Scales New Peak; While ADTO Declines

demand_drivers.description: A robust ecosystem of IPOs and secondary market activity supports a high number of listed companies, reflecting strong investor confidence and corporate fundraising.

market_sizing.methodology: Total count of companies listed on India's primary stock exchanges, NSE and BSE, as of FY26. This indicates the depth and breadth of the public capital markets, directly relevant to exchanges and data providers.
